explanation: The grandfather of Ephraim and Manasseh, son of Isaac and father of Joseph. One of the patriarchs in the Bible.
Jacob's eldest son with Rachel, brother to Benjamin and half-brother to his other siblings. An important figure in Genesis who becomes governor of Egypt.
The younger son of Joseph and Asenath, grandson of Jacob. He and his descendants become one of Israel's twelve tribes.
The older son of Joseph and Asenath, grandson of Jacob. He and his descendants also become one of Israel's twelve tribes.
A positive statement or action performed by God or people, often to ask for prosperity, protection, or happiness for someone.
The name given to Jacob after his struggle with an angel. It also refers to the united people of Jacob's twelve sons and their descendants.
To take in a child from another family and treat them as one's own child. In Genesis 48, Jacob adopts Joseph's two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh.
Symbolizes strength, authority, and honor. In this context, Jacob places his right hand on Ephraim's head to bless him.
An action performed by Jacob when he blesses his grandsons, Ephraim and Manasseh. This symbolizes that Ephraim, though younger, will become greater than his older brother Manasseh.
